name: The Ashen Marches
description: A burned borderland of black heath, broken keeps and roads that run east toward Highspire. The last war passed through twelve years ago and the grass has never grown back right; now the Thornwake's refugees come south across it, and the briars come after them. What is left of the Order of Ash keeps to its last tower and does not ride out.
travel_text: Grey ash puffs up from every footstep, and the wind smells of old fires and coming snow.

events.text: The sky goes the colour of a bruise and the wind lifts the whole heath into the air. Ash fills your mouth and eyes.

success.message: You find the lee of a fallen wall and wait it out with your cloak over your face. When it passes, the world is new and grey and you are none the worse.

fail.message: You stumble blind for an hour and come out coughing, scraped from a fall you never saw coming.

events.text: A family from the north sits beside a cart with a cracked axle. The father is trying to lift it alone. The children watch the road behind them, not you.

success.message: You get your shoulder under the bed and the wheel back on its pin. The mother presses a twist of honey brittle on you and will not hear no.

fail.message: The axle splits the rest of the way. You help them shift what they can carry onto their backs, and they walk on south without the cart.

events.text: A grey warhorse in rotted caparison stands alone on a rise, saddled, bridled, waiting for a rider who is not coming.

success.message: It lets you close enough to read the faded ember on its harness: an Order mount, gone feral. In the saddlebag, a purse and a stale wrapped ration. The horse watches you take them, then turns and trots away east.

fail.message: It bares its teeth, wheels, and is gone over the rise before you are close.

events.text: Hoofprints, a lot of them, leave the road and cross the heath toward a stand of burned pines.

success.message: The trail ends at a cairn of stones that is too neat to be natural. Underneath: a reaver's stash of coin and a flask of something strong.

fail.message: The trail splits, doubles back and disappears into ash. Whoever made it did not want company.

events.text: The wind brings voices from the north-east, many of them, singing the same three notes over and over. It is almost pretty.

success.message: It is a hymn, slowed down until it sounds like breathing. You fix its direction: a hollow among the dead pines, two hours past the refugee camp.

fail.message: You catch yourself humming the three notes an hour later and cannot remember when you started.

events.text: A milestone carved with the Order's ember stands half sunk in ash. Under the ember, somebody has cut a long column of small names.

success.message: They are the names of the knights who stayed at Greyford when the horn blew. Ser Halvard Grey's is first. Fresh ash has been brushed off them, carefully, by a hand bigger than yours.

fail.message: The names are too worn to read, and the ash fills them in again as you watch.

sights: a burned keep on a ridge, its windows like empty eye sockets
a field of black stumps where an orchard used to be
a line of refugees on the horizon, small as ants, walking south
a crow picking at a rusted helm
red ember lilies growing straight out of the ash
a briar coiled round a signpost so tight the wood has split
snow and ash falling together, so you cannot tell which is which
a ruined wayshrine with fresh wildflowers on the step
